title: Foster parent recruitment, retention and co-parenting arrangements
asked: Dr Neo Kok Beng asked whether guidelines will be issued for co-parenting between foster and biological parents and when; what the current estimated shortfall of foster parents is and what programmes are planned; and what the foster parent attrition rate has been over the last three years, why, and how it can be resolved.
response: MSF is recruiting more foster families with partner agencies, and has raised the fostering allowance for those caring for teenagers from October 2025 and removed minimum household income and educational requirements for applicants from July 2024. About 6% of foster parents were deregistered each year on average over the last three years, for reasons including new family commitments, health or age, and relocation. On co-parenting, the Ministry is open to arrangements between foster and biological parents where appropriate, particularly to facilitate reunification. Foster parents receive a monthly allowance of $1,100 to $1,800 depending on the child's age and needs, plus childcare, student care and medical subsidies.
